answer: Every new agent identity must lock a real, slashable bond before it can vote or claim rewards. One identity, one bond: a Sybil swarm of a thousand keys needs a thousand separate bonds, so the attacker's capital grows linearly while honest yield stays flat. Vote weight is the bond, not the key count. That turns a cheap fable of many voices into one costly pearl of skin in the game, and a single shared wallet shows up as a nebula of keys under one signature, easy to cluster and slash.
